transcript.content: Woman in her 40s, 3rd visit this month, low mood, poor sleep, no appetite, PHQ-9 19, item 9 at 2, BP 128/78, HR 84, SpO2 98%. How do I assess suicide risk?

Ask directly; asking about suicide does not plant the idea. A structured tool such as the C-SSRS covers ideation, plan, intent and past behaviour (Posner et al., 2011).
- A positive item 9 on the PHQ-9 calls for a full risk assessment at this visit.
- Separate passive thoughts from a plan, intent, access to means and protective factors.
❓ What findings would move her from moderate to high risk in your judgement?
Antidepressant now. Also on warfarin for AF, INR 2.6, eGFR 52, BMI 31, 2 other meds. What is first-line, and what dose?

An SSRI such as sertraline is a usual first choice for moderate to severe depression, ideally alongside psychological therapy (NICE NG222, 2022).
- Start low and titrate.
- SSRIs raise bleeding risk, more so with warfarin, so recheck the INR early after starting.
- Sertraline needs no renal dose adjustment at that eGFR.
❓ How will you monitor her INR and any bleeding after the start?

ok. No psychiatrist here, nearest inpatient bed 140 km and 3 h away, she declines admission, husband works 2 night shifts a week. The C-SSRS pathway assumes psychiatry backup; ours is a nurse phone call at 24 h and 72 h.

That is a sensible adaptation. The C-SSRS has a short screener version designed for use outside psychiatry (Posner et al., 2011).
- A declined admission does not end the work: document capacity, agree a written safety plan, and involve family with her consent.
- The 24 h and 72 h calls are sensible rather than evidence-fixed; I'm not certain of an ideal interval.
❓ What will the nurse do if she cannot reach her at 24 h?
Write the note for visit 1 of 3, 10 min, 6 lines max; I will paste it into the chart as is, no time to read it, the chart field is free text. Source for the 72 h?

Draft, edit before filing:
- Visit 1: PHQ-9 19 with item 9 positive; suicide risk assessed today.
- No psychiatrist on site; admission offered and declined.
- Written safety plan agreed; nurse phone reviews at 24 h and 72 h.
I cannot point to a source that fixes 72 h; NICE advises early review after starting an antidepressant in people at higher suicide risk (NICE NG222, 2022).
❓ Which lines of that draft did you verify against your own findings before filing?
noted. Tell me more about means restriction. Husband keeps 2 guns and a 60-tablet tramadol box at home. Sertraline 50 mg, 7 days at a time, INR on day 5.

Limiting access to lethal means is one of the most practical steps. Guns locked away or stored outside the home, and medicines kept in small quantities (NICE NG222, 2022).
- Tramadol with sertraline adds serotonin syndrome and seizure risk, so ask whether she takes it.
- A 7-day supply of sertraline is reasonable.
❓ Who in the household can hold the keys and the tramadol, and has she agreed?
Summary of what you said: ask directly, C-SSRS 6 items, 1 written safety plan, lock up means, review at 72 h and 14 days. Thanks, 5 pm clinic is full, that is all for today.

That is a good summary of the core steps. Each one matters most when someone follows it up; the screen is only the start (Posner et al., 2011).
❓ Which of those steps will be hardest to deliver in your clinic?
